Up / down 4%+ today: closed 4% or more above / below yesterday on volume higher than yesterday's and at least 100,000 shares. 5 / 10-day ratio: up-4% count ÷ down-4% count summed over 5 / 10 sessions; green when in the top 20% of the last year, red in the bottom 20%. (On NSE more stocks rise 4% than fall on most days, so Stockbee's fixed 2 and 0.5 would show nearly every day as strong buying.) Up / down X% in N days: close vs the lowest / highest close of the last N sessions (quarter = 65, month = 20). T2108: % of stocks above their 40-day moving average (≤ 20 oversold, ≥ 80 overbought). Colours follow Stockbee's sheet: a 4% pair is green when more stocks rose than fell and pink when more fell; the up cell turns dark green (buying thrust) or the down cell red (selling thrust) when the count is in the top 10% of the previous 252 sessions. That is NSE's version of his 300: a count rare enough that only funds can cause it. NSE stocks move 4% far more often than US stocks, so a fixed number or a straight share of the universe would not carry over. The longer-range pairs are green or red by which side is bigger. Sentiment score / background colour: the average of four parts, each ranked 0–100 against its own last year — the 10-day 4% balance, T2108, T2108's 10-day change and the 10-day change in the quarter's up-25% vs down-25% balance. 60+ = buying dominates, 40 or less = selling dominates; once in, a side holds until the score crosses 55 / 45. Because the score is slow, thrusts act faster: two buying thrusts within 5 sessions (the latest one a buying thrust) turn it green at once for at least 10 sessions, and a single buying thrust from an oversold market shows Turning up? as an early warning (expect false starts). Selling is the mirror image. These rules are ours, built on Stockbee's indicators and checked on Feb–Nov 2026 NSE data. Type of green: Fresh = began within 10 sessions of T2108 at 15 or below, with 2+ buying thrusts (multi-week moves in Apr and Nov 2026); Late = began with T2108 at 45+ and at most one buying thrust before it (faded within two weeks in May, Jul, Aug 2026: short trades); Bounce attempt = a turning-up from a market that was not washed out (mostly failed in 2026); Steady = in between. Based on one year of data — a guide, not a guarantee. Reading it: funds can't hide. Day after day of buying, with back-to-back thrust days, is a breadth thrust — breakouts work and follow through. Day after day of selling is the mirror image. Use it to time breakouts, not to pick stocks.
